play: open
This is Mempire, live on Monad testnet. Every coin is a fighter, and that strip is Monad itself: blocks voted in about three hundred milliseconds, and final in under six hundred.
signin
Sign-up is one passkey prompt, through Mera. No seed phrase, no extension.
deck
In about ten seconds, the relayer mints an eight-card starter deck on chain, with test AUSD and a little MON for gas.
mint
Minting a new fighter pulls a live Pyth price into the same transaction.
stake
The side boards are the market meta, written on chain by Chainlink CRE. We stake the one-dollar tier in MON, and queue a ranked match.
battle
Every card I drop is its own Monad transaction, signed by a per-match session key, so there are no popups. Each pill shows the real round trip: executed, then final.
tower
We fast-forward. And a tower falls.
result
Pot secured! The second player's claim settles the pot on chain: ninety percent to the winner, plus a chest.
clans
Clans and clan wars score only staked wins verified on chain. These clans were seeded by our team for the demo.
empire
Empire holds the leaderboard, reads Monad's staking precompile live, and verifies a passkey signature with Monad's P-256 precompile.
how: So, what is live on Monad?
Chainlink CRE writes the market meta: thirty-six fighters, signed by the workflow, accepted only from its forwarder.
Pyth prices every mint, verified on chain in the same transaction.
Gasless chests: an EIP-7702 authorization, our own paymaster, and the canonical EntryPoint. The player spends no MON.
Passkeys, checked by Monad's P-256 precompile, at a fraction of the gas.
Every card you play is logged on chain, from a session key.
And every staked match is settled by the contract itself.
Six power-ups. All live on Monad testnet.
outro: Mempire. Every coin is a fighter. Play now, at mempire monad, dot vercel, dot app.
